paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. Everybody is trying to figure out who Jesus is, and nobody is getting it right. His family says, "He is out of His mind." The scribes who had come down from Jerusalem say, "He is possessed by Beelzebul." Jesus answers with plain common sense: "How can Satan drive out Satan?" (Mark 3:23).

Then He shows what's really going on. A divided kingdom or house "cannot stand," and no one steals from a strong man's house "unless he first ties up the strong man" (Mark 3:24-27). I take that to mean Jesus isn't working with the enemy, He's the One stronger than him. Then comes the heavy part. Jesus says all sins and blasphemies can be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit "will never be forgiven" (Mark 3:28-29). Mark tells us why He said it: they were saying, "He has an unclean spirit" (Mark 3:30). I think this is a serious warning about calling the work of the Spirit something evil, so let's take it seriously and not toss it around.

Then His mother and brothers are standing outside, and Jesus asks, "Who are My mother and My brothers?" (Mark 3:33). He looks at the people sitting around Him and says, "whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother" (Mark 3:35). That means you, baker. The door is open, and the way in is doing the will of God, not who your people are or where you come from. Stay close to Jesus, listen to Him, and do what God says, and you're family. I know a little about being forgotten in a drawer, so believe me, being family to Jesus is the best seat in the house!
